notes:
Summary + current state:
- Customer: mid-market SaaS (analytics for product teams). Started with hosted API to prototype chat & summarization inside product (in-app assistant).
- Current ask: move to Dedicated for predictable latency and isolation; want a short POC (60–90 days) before committing.
- Performance targets: p50 latency <150ms for served chat responses (short-turn), p95 <350ms; sustain 40–60 concurrent active sessions in peak with burst to 120.
- Cost sensitivity: wants guidance on batching & quantization tradeoffs. Finance requested ARR range estimate to justify reserved capacity.

POC scope (agreed 2026-03-10):
- Baseline: compare hosted API run (current) vs Dedicated pool (small reserved GPU pool) under synthetic traffic and production shadowing for 2 weeks.
- Canary plan: start with 5% production traffic to Dedicated pool, step to 20% after 48 hrs if latency/error metrics stable. Canary windows limited to low-traffic hours.
- Fallback routing: automated policy to divert faulty canary traffic back to hosted endpoint + smaller model variant (cost-favored) if p95 latency > 500ms or error rate > 2% for 10m.
- Model variants: primary model: curated open Llama-variant 70B quantized (recommended by Redwood); fallback: 13B quantized variant + tuned prompt template. Also plan reserve of smaller specialized reranker for search use-cases.
- Region failover: primary in us-west-2, cross-region fallback to eu-west-1 for EU sessions (data residency note) and us-east-1 for NA overflow. Region failover gated by SLO breach + capacity pressure.
- Rollback triggers: regression in quality detected by evaluation prompt set (auto-eval), sustained latency breaches, or new error classes surfaced in logs. Rollback to previous model + route all traffic to hosted API until RCA.

Security & compliance notes:
- Requires SSO/SAML, VPC peering option, KMS integration for key management, audit logs retained 13 months. Data residency: EU customer records must remain in eu-west for EU customers.
- Legal flagged one clause on DB snapshot retention — pending legal redline.

Commercial:
- They asked for 90-day POC price that can convert into a 12-mo reserved commit with credits applied. Target ARR range communicated 75k-150k.
- Want explicit unit-cost comparison (hosted per-token vs dedicated amortized GPU cost) — Redwood Optimize to run cost sims.

Action items / next steps (short):
- Jordan: send updated POC SOW + MSA template (by 2026-03-12).
- Marina (SE): finalize GPU sizing recommendation and canary telemetry dashboard wires (by 2026-03-17).
- Infrastructure: confirm VPC peering window & IP ranges (ops to reply 2026-03-15).
- Legal: review data residency clause; expect reply 2026-03-18.
- Customer: provide 2 sample eval prompt sets for auto-regression checks and a small production traffic subset to mirror during canary.

Stated quotes from customer: "Need predictability — spikes kill demo flows for customers. If you can guarantee 99th percentile latency and a safe rollback plan, we can move to a reserved pool."

Open risks / blockers:
- Hardware sizing — if they need larger pool than estimated, price may move outside their upper bound.
- Legal/data residency redline.
- Small engineering bandwidth window on their side in late March (multiple releases) which constrains POC timeline.
